questions.q: Tell me about the design work you have done. What did you design, which tools did you use, and for which clients or brands?
questions.looks_for: Real projects (social posts, logos, brochures, packaging), tools like Photoshop, Illustrator, Canva, Figma, CorelDRAW, and their role.

questions.q: Describe a design project you are proud of. What was the brief, how did you approach it, and what was the result?
questions.looks_for: Clear brief, process (ideas, drafts, feedback), design choices explained, and the outcome or client response.

questions.q: What is the difference between designing for print and designing for social media?
questions.looks_for: Print: CMYK, high resolution, bleed and margins; digital: RGB, screen sizes, lighter files; mentions checking final size.

questions.q: How do you use colour, font and spacing to make the most important message stand out in a poster?
questions.looks_for: Visual hierarchy: size and weight for main message, contrast colour, limited fonts, white space, clear flow for the eye.

questions.q: Why is it wrong to use images or fonts found on Google in client work, and what do you use instead?
questions.looks_for: Copyright and licence issues; uses licensed stock, free-licence sources, client photos, or own work and checks font licences.

questions.q: A client keeps asking for changes after the fourth revision and now wants the logo 'bigger' and 'more modern' in the same day. What would you do?
questions.looks_for: Stays polite, asks for examples to clarify, explains revision limits from the agreement, offers options, and keeps the deadline in view.

questions.q: Why do you want this graphic designer job, when can you join (state your notice period), and what salary do you expect?
questions.looks_for: Clear reason linked to the work, states notice period or joining date in days or weeks, and gives an expected monthly or yearly salary figure or range without dodging.
